evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The Bootstrap Planning Ledger is durable planning/source state for feature-spec conversations. It is not assistant memory, not Plan Mode, and not canonical Plans prose. Canonical product/build truth remains live non-pipeline Plans docs after compilation.

items.impact: Prevents ledger, assistant state, generated artifacts, or source-lineage material from displacing live canonical Plans.
items.statement: PLS-001 and the prologue establish a clear, testable authority split between durable planning memory and canonical product truth.
items.title: Ledger authority is explicitly bounded

evidence.exact_quote: - Bootstrap records can be imported into the native service without losing record identity, source refs, decisions, questions, blockers, corrections, or gui_related classification.

items.impact: Builders must invent format-version negotiation, collision handling, and a measurable losslessness oracle, allowing incompatible imports to claim compliance.
items.statement: Import/export compatibility is required, but the PlanUnit does not define version negotiation, identity-collision policy, downgrade behavior, or a round-trip equivalence test.
items.title: Bootstrap-native migration remains under-specified

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Bootstrap ledger state uses JSONL append logs and JSON state projections. Source shards preserve exact source/history for recovery, audit, and migration; shards are cold source/history, not the active operating interface.

items.impact: Exact historical material can persist indefinitely without defined retention, redaction, access, deletion, or backup propagation behavior.
items.statement: The cold-source role is clear, but its privacy lifecycle and destructive-action semantics are absent.
items.title: Cold source shards lack a data lifecycle

evidence.exact_quote: - The operating capsule names allowed reads, allowed writes, and forbidden governance outputs.

items.impact: An implementation can merely describe permissions without enforcing path confinement, rejecting tampered capsules, or recording violations.
items.statement: Allowed and forbidden surfaces are named, but capsule authenticity, path validation, enforcement failure, and violation observability are not specified.
items.title: Operating-capsule permissions have no enforcement semantics

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Conversational planning captures neutral design_atom records. The compiler converts accepted atoms into PlanUnits later. Ledger records preserve exact field names, examples, negative constraints, compatibility-only notes, stale/retired notes, owner hints, user corrections, and agent-inferred gui_related true/false.

items.impact: Verbatim preservation can retain secrets, personal data, malicious instructions, or prohibited content with no defined quarantine or redaction lineage.
items.statement: The exact-preservation obligation has no exception and provenance contract for secrets, personal data, or adversarial source content.
items.title: Exact preservation conflicts with safe data handling

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: After every substantive ledger conversation turn, append one event, upsert affected records, update questions/blockers/corrections, and rewrite state/current.json, state/handoff.json, state/open_items.json, and state/compile_queue.json projections. Multiple simultaneous ledgers are tracked by stable ledger_id values in ledger_registry.json.

items.impact: A crash or concurrent writer can leave event, record, and projection surfaces divergent while still appearing resumable.
items.statement: The bootstrap per-turn protocol orders multiple writes but defines no lock, transaction marker, CAS, idempotency, partial-write state, or rollback/replay procedure.
items.title: Bootstrap turn writes are not atomic

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Owner ambiguity is normal during planning. The ledger captures candidate owners, consumer docs, evidence, and adjudication rules; compile agents resolve ordinary row-level placement by evidence and deterministic policy, asking Jared only for a true product decision.

items.impact: Different agents can make different owner choices from the same evidence and still claim deterministic compliance.
items.statement: The document invokes deterministic policy without specifying precedence, tie-breaking, required evidence, or an oracle for distinguishing ordinary ambiguity from a product decision.
items.title: Owner adjudication is deterministic in name only

evidence.exact_quote: - Planning Wizard/native Goal integration respects the ledger-to-Plan and Plan-to-node boundaries.

items.impact: The future integration can expose ambiguous progress or retry behavior when transfer, conversion, or audit fails across boundaries.
items.statement: The integration boundary is stated, but invocation identity, cancellation, retry, partial success, and visible failure-state propagation are not defined.
items.title: Planning Wizard and Goal integration lacks failure semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Registry, manifest, compile queue, and handoff paths agree on the same ledger_id and phase.

items.impact: Provides a concrete cross-surface consistency condition before a ledger is usable.
items.statement: The required file layout, existence gate, and shared ledger identity/phase oracle are explicit.
items.title: Bootstrap directory usability has a concrete identity check

evidence.exact_quote: - Validator output reports exact errors and warnings instead of allowing false completion.

items.impact: Structural drift and hidden YAML overwrite conditions are required to fail rather than produce false completion.
items.statement: PLS-010 enumerates concrete validator failures and requires exact diagnostic reporting through dedicated validation surfaces.
items.title: Ledger validation is explicitly falsifiable

evidence.exact_quote: - Ordinary compile does not update Spec_Lock, shards, evidence bundles, plan_graph, auto_decisions, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, final build tasks, or production build tasks.

items.impact: Prevents ordinary planning compilation from silently mutating governance or creating executable work.
items.statement: Compile-queue fidelity, pending-seal state, and forbidden downstream artifacts are sharply separated.
items.title: Ordinary compile has an explicit terminal boundary

evidence.exact_quote: repair_required_count is zero or a true user decision is required. Passing

items.impact: Parallel audits or repairs can race on closure status, evidence hashes, or reopen decisions and lose a valid transition.
items.statement: The closure workflow is semantically exhaustive but does not define append/update atomicity, revision checks, lock ownership, duplicate-writer handling, or crash recovery for the global registry.
items.title: Semantic closure registry lacks concurrency control

evidence.exact_quote: The doc_impact_matrix rule forbids owner-only repairs: Do not update only the obvious owner docs while leaving stale references in consumer/index/UI docs.

items.impact: A required compile input can be absent, incomplete, or stale while current named validation still passes.
items.statement: The matrices carry strong coverage requirements, but the only matrix-specific validation surface is future work, leaving no current executable completeness oracle in this PlanUnit.
items.title: Compile-input matrices are required but not currently enforceable

evidence.exact_quote: - No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, GoalRuns, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, or production build tasks are created by this compile.

items.impact: Different GUI surfaces can present stale or contradictory readiness, hide offline durability failure, or offer inaccessible recovery actions while honoring the backend boundary.
items.statement: PLS-014 is gui_related and defines ledger_sync_blocked behavior, but it does not specify the visible status, disabled-control semantics, accessible announcement, localization, offline distinction, or recovery affordance.
items.title: Ledger synchronization failure has no complete GUI truth contract

evidence.exact_quote: - ledger_sync_blocked clears only after append log, records, projections, and handoff/currentness state agree.

items.impact: Native implementations must preserve atomic turn durability, CAS/idempotency, and a measurable blocked-state clearance invariant.
items.statement: The native runtime contract explicitly addresses atomicity, concurrent revision control, idempotency, partial-write blocking, referential integrity, and recovery clearance.
items.title: Native ledger durability and recovery are strongly specified

evidence.exact_quote: - ExternalRepoFinding records have finding_key, upstream_url, observed_state, PM disposition, reopen conditions, and freshness window.

items.impact: External findings can diverge between the semantic closure registry and a new external registry, or collide across upstream repositories.
items.statement: PLS-016 defines useful fields but not the authoritative storage owner, repository-scoped key identity, or merge/reuse relationship with the existing semantic closure registry and the later PLS-017/PLS-018 concepts.
items.title: External finding closure has an unresolved registry seam

evidence.exact_quote: - import_package rejects path traversal, absolute paths, symlink escape, package-size overflow, expanded-size overflow, and ledger id/name collision unless explicit replace or keep-both policy is recorded.

items.impact: Constrains common archive/package attacks, resource expansion abuse, and destructive identity collisions at the storage boundary.
items.statement: The in-process service boundary and import-package threat checks are explicit, including collision policy requirements.
items.title: Native import security is concretely bounded

items.impact: A technically visible reason can still be inaccessible, untranslated, unactionable, or misleading about confidence, evidence, actor, and reopen options.
items.statement: User visibility is required, but the displayed closure contract has no required fields, accessible announcement behavior, localization handling, or recovery/reopen affordance.
items.title: Bot closure visibility is not a usable GUI contract

items.impact: Builders cannot implement or test the P1 requirement without inventing evidence sufficiency, states, transitions, authority, actors, timestamps, reopen triggers, and deduplication behavior.
items.statement: PLS-018 names an ExternalIssueClosureRegistry and two fragments of acceptance behavior but provides no record schema, state machine, authority model, persistence owner, evidence-quality rule, or executable validator.
items.title: P1 external issue closure is not implementation-ready

segments.summary: Reviewed the authority boundary, bootstrap/native compatibility, machine-first storage, compact resume surface, atom preservation, per-turn writes, owner adjudication, Goal integration, and deterministic directory contract. The strongest adversarial risks are unsafe exact preservation, non-atomic bootstrap writes, unenforced capsule permissions, and underspecified migration equivalence.

Reviewed validator behavior, compile/seal separation, semantic closure durability, and required compile-input matrices. Validator and phase boundaries are strong; registry concurrency and currently executable matrix-completeness checks remain material gaps.

Reviewed planning-product synchronization, native runtime durability, external-upstream closure records, the hardened in-process storage/API boundary, and user-visible AI closure confidence. Native atomicity and import defenses are strong; GUI failure truth, registry authority/deduplication, accessibility, and localization are incomplete.

Reviewed the P1 external issue closure PlanUnit. Its stated intent is valid, but it lacks the schema, state machine, authority, persistence, and validator detail required for implementation or falsification.
